title: Specific cleavage of 5' overhangs of non-target strand by Cas9 activated by target DNA binding.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the single Zenodo file (Lv_Unprocessed_gels_and_statistical_Sourcedata.zip, 1,427,340 bytes, CC-BY-4.0), unzipped it, and read every sheet of the one spreadsheet inside. It holds 10 sheets of per-figure numbers: 236 rows containing any number at all, 2,032 numeric cells in total, of which 127 rows are quantitative PCR amplification traces (fluorescence versus cycle number) for ~8 target concentrations. The other 7 files are PDF scans of unprocessed gels (Fig1-4, FigS2-S4), not quantified tables.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the DNA substrate sequences are listed in Supplementary Table S1; I could not retrieve the publisher supplement (Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint timed out twice, so supplement not retrievable). The assay conditions (400 nM target DNA, 50 nM SpCas9, 250 nM single guide RNA, 37C, 0-60 min, 15% denaturing gel, bands quantified in ImageJ) are from the methods section, not from the files.

a1_downloadable.note: Open Zenodo record, CC-BY 4.0, no login. Download was very slow (needed a resumed range request) but completed: 1.4 MB zip opened fine.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Cleavage percentages and fluorescence ratios are present as numbers, but each sheet is a free-form figure panel block (merged headers, panel codes like '11T', '1-2', 'H840A') with no shared key column; a feature/label table would have to be hand-assembled panel by panel.

a3_inputs_present.note: No DNA or guide RNA sequence appears anywhere in the data files. Rows are keyed by figure shorthand ('WT', '3-4', '21T') that must be mapped by hand to Supplementary Table S1, which I could not retrieve.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are mostly labelled in-sheet: percent cleaved from gel grey values, 'F1/F0' fluorescence ratios, 'Cq values', copies per microlitre concentrations, cycle numbers.

a5_enough_rows.note: Counted in the file: 236 rows with any numeric value, and only ~65 of those are distinct cleavage conditions (8 in Fig1, 11 in Fig3, 15 in Fig4, 31 in Fig5), each in 2-3 replicates. The checklist needs ~1,500 labelled rows, or ~400 for classification.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Sheet names map one-to-one onto the paper's figure panels and the triplicate structure matches the methods; nothing contradicts the text.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels are physical measurements: band grey values from denaturing gels quantified in ImageJ, plus fluorescence and quantitative PCR readouts. No model output anywhere.

existing_models.name: DeepSpCas9 (convolutional neural network predicting SpCas9 cutting activity from target sequence, Science Advances 2019)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported the highest Spearman rank correlation of nine published models across seven held-out test sets, per the paper abstract I retrieved via search; I did not open the weights or rerun it.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not read - I only retrieved the abstract-level summary, so I am not citing a discussion sentence.

backbone.name: Nucleotide Transformer or DNABERT-2 (DNA language models) would be the natural fit for short double-stranded DNA substrates
backbone.hardware: CPU laptop would suffice for ~65 short sequences, but 65 examples cannot train or honestly evaluate any head
backbone.licence: Not checked - moot given the row count

integration.partner_dataset: None identified that joins: the data carries no accession, no genomic coordinate and no sequence, only figure-panel shorthand.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written - there is no identifier in the files to join on.

controls.positive_control: The paper's own D10A RuvC-domain mutant, which shows zero cleavage, would be the obvious signal a model must recover - but with 3 enzyme variants it is a sanity check, not a control for a model.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is runnable in principle but meaningless at ~65 conditions.
controls.external_validation: None - no second lab has measured 5' overhang non-target-strand cleavage, since this paper reports it for the first time.

honest_claim_h3: With 65 hand-curated conditions from one lab, one enzyme and a handful of synthetic oligonucleotides, no model could claim more than 'it memorised this figure set'.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the sequence around a DNA cut site to predict how much Cas9 trims the single-stranded overhang next to it.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would show the model each synthetic double-stranded DNA substrate (overhang length, overhang base composition, the extra protospacer adjacent motif in the 5' region, and guide-RNA mismatch positions) and learn from the measured cleavage. I verified only ~65 distinct conditions exist, in 2-3 replicates each.
plain_idea.predict: Percent of the non-target strand overhang cut, taken from the brightness of bands on denaturing gels measured in ImageJ, plus fluorescence ratios from a reporter assay.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups building Cas9-based diagnostics and worrying about unintended trimming at edited sites would want to know which flanking sequences trigger this newly reported side activity; with this few measurements, nothing can be learned beyond what the figures already show.

more_or_better_data.why: DeepSpCas9 and similar sequence-activity models were trained on tens of thousands of measured target sites; this dataset has ~65 conditions, and they measure a different readout (overhang trimming, not double-strand cut efficiency).

confidence_score.why: Replicates exist (2-3 per condition) so measurement noise is estimable, but 65 conditions is far too few groups to calibrate per-prediction uncertainty.

models_beatable.why: No model exists for this specific side activity, so there is nothing to beat; the adjacent sgRNA-activity models (DeepSpCas9, 2019, convolutional network) are old but solve a different problem and cannot be compared on these numbers.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No existing model takes these inputs and produces this output, so it cannot be run as a baseline, and there is no public data measuring the same quantity the same way to add.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predict percent cleavage of the non-target-strand 5' overhang from substrate sequence features (overhang length, base identity, upstream protospacer adjacent motif presence, guide-RNA mismatch position), with a frozen DNA language model plus a small regression head. Dead on sample size.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: the spreadsheet is 37 KB and parsed in under a second with openpyxl; the 8 hours is the hand-work of mapping ~65 figure-panel labels to sequences in a supplement I could not retrieve.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the distinct measured conditions in the source-data spreadsheet. I did this: 236 numeric rows, of which 127 are quantitative PCR amplification traces and only ~65 are distinct cleavage conditions - roughly 6 times too few even for a classification task.

verdict_reason: Figure source data only: ~65 distinct measured conditions, no sequences in the files, no joinable key - fails A5, A3 and A2.
